problem_text:
A city planner needs to allocate the annual infrastructure budget across 17 different project categories to maximize the total expected community benefit score. The characteristics of each project category are as follows:
* Category A: expected benefit is 0.065, disruption index is 0.121, allocation bounds [0.001, 0.562]
* Category B: expected benefit is 0.071, disruption index is 0.258, allocation bounds [0.050, 0.453]
* Category C: expected benefit is 0.101, disruption index is 0.230, allocation bounds [0.073, 0.848]
* Category D: expected benefit is 0.134, disruption index is 0.277, allocation bounds [0.049, 0.733]
* Category E: expected benefit is 0.069, disruption index is 0.183, allocation bounds [0.093, 0.606]
* Category F: expected benefit is 0.161, disruption index is 0.054, allocation bounds [0.094, 0.593]
* Category G: expected benefit is 0.034, disruption index is 0.221, allocation bounds [0.097, 0.713]
* Category H: expected benefit is 0.195, disruption index is 0.085, allocation bounds [0.037, 0.718]
* Category I: expected benefit is 0.092, disruption index is 0.144, allocation bounds [0.049, 0.691]
* Category J: expected benefit is 0.050, disruption index is 0.142, allocation bounds [0.064, 0.856]
* Category K: expected benefit is 0.099, disruption index is 0.119, allocation bounds [0.059, 0.741]
* Category L: expected benefit is 0.111, disruption index is 0.186, allocation bounds [0.041, 0.445]
* Category M: expected benefit is 0.152, disruption index is 0.031, allocation bounds [0.004, 0.321]
* Category N: expected benefit is 0.157, disruption index is 0.050, allocation bounds [0.092, 0.788]
* Category O: expected benefit is 0.168, disruption index is 0.146, allocation bounds [0.038, 0.679]
* Category P: expected benefit is 0.163, disruption index is 0.055, allocation bounds [0.057, 0.706]
* Category Q: expected benefit is 0.024, disruption index is 0.065, allocation bounds [0.019, 0.718]

Each category must receive a budget proportion that falls within its specified bounds, and the total allocation across all categories must sum to one. To ensure adequate coverage of essential services, the planner requires that high-priority categories, represented by the subset H = {A, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L, M, N, O, P, Q}, collectively receive at least 0.746 of the total budget. Additionally, the overall portfolio disruption index must not exceed 0.172, and the total expected community benefit must be no less than 0.095. Determine the optimal budget allocation that maximizes the total expected benefit while satisfying all constraints.
